prompt:
Build a single-file HTML5 game, "Marigold Park": a pixel-art 3D baseball game on a floating voxel island, where you manage one of two teams (you choose the approach, the pitches, the defence and the steals; the sim plays out each pitch). three.js r128 from cdnjs, no build step for the player, everything inline, no asset files.

LOOK
Render the 3D scene to a low-res target (default 2 px art pixels, slider 1-6), then a post pass: depth-based outlines, snap every pixel to a fixed 90-colour OKLab palette, Bayer dither. Orthographic isometric camera (rotate in 45 degree steps or drag, zoom, tilt) placed 850 m from its target with a far plane of 1700, so the island is never clipped at low tilt. Sun shadow map, day / dusk / night with eased light changes and floodlights that come on after dusk.
Island: a slab of 2.4 m voxel columns (about 208 x 192 m), terraced rim, banded soil and slate, a waterfall. The slab is solid right through the centre (every cell included) with DoubleSide faces, so no hole shows from any camera angle. A 2048 px painted ground: outer grass patchwork, the park (mown stripes, fair and foul ground, warning track, infield dirt skin, grass diamond, base paths, circles, chalk lines), and the village (paths, plaza, parking, playground, pond, stream).
Park geometry in metres, home plate at the origin: bases 18 m apart, mound 13.5 m out, fence 60 m at the lines swelling to 70 m at centre (3 m high), foul poles, backstop, two dugouts with benches, bullpens, umpires, base coaches and an on-deck batter. Three playing surfaces that repaint the ground and change the physics: natural grass, artificial turf (the ball skips and keeps rolling, fewer bad hops), red clay infield (slow and heavy but more bad hops and errors).
Stands in eight side groups around the park: coloured seat sections, a brick concourse wall with pilasters, windows and a cornice, a striped canopy with a scalloped valance over the back rows, a press box, an outfield scoreboard, outfield bleachers beyond the fence, advertising boards, banners, bunting, rails, pennant poles at the corners, vendors in the aisles, a mascot by the third-base dugout, floodlight towers, thousands of instanced spectators in team colours who cheer on big plays.
Village around the park: plaza with a gate arch and sign, ticket booths, a statue of a batter on a pedestal, a fountain, market stalls with umbrellas, benches, lamps, hedges, planters, a car park, a playground, a pond, a stream with a waterfall, groves, walkers and floating islets.
Doll's-house lift: the eight stand sides that face the camera rise out of the way (with their crowds and fence) and ease back when the camera turns; disabled for cinematic cameras and between innings; toggle "Lift near stands".

GAME
Six invented teams (Harbor Gulls, Cedar Bears, Ironwood Foxes, Riverton Rays, Maple Hawks, Dunes Lizards) with generated rosters: 9 hitters (C, 1B, 2B, SS, 3B, LF, CF, RF, DH) with contact, power, eye, speed, range, arm, glove and handedness (R / L / switch), plus 4 pitchers (a starter with 70-90 pitches of stamina and three relievers with about 30) with velocity, control, movement and a repertoire from fastball, slider, curve and changeup. Block-built people with caps, helmets, gloves, bats, catcher's gear, umpires; poses for windup, delivery, swing, bunt, run, slide, throw and catch.
Formats: Quick (3 innings), Short (5), Full (9). Ties after the last inning go to extra innings (the previous batter starts on second base, up to three extra innings), walk-offs end the game on the spot.
Fixed-step 60 Hz sim. Each pitch: windup, release, flight with break per pitch type (fatigue worsens control past about 80% of the pitcher's stamina), a strike zone 0.6 m wide and 0.78 m tall, umpire calls with a small error rate on borderline pitches. Challenges: each side has 2; when a borderline call goes against the team you manage you get a 4.5 s window to challenge (key C); an electronic strike-zone overlay then shows the truth; the AI challenges wrong calls with high probability.
Batting: approach Contact / Power / Patient / Bunt, aim Auto / Pull / Center / Oppo. By default the sim swings for you using timing windows scaled by the hitter's contact skill; or tick "Time the swing myself" and press Space with windows widened. Batted-ball physics with gravity, drag, wind, bounces, rolling, fence hits and home runs; wind modes Calm, Out to centre (+8% carry), In from centre (-10%); the surface changes bounce and roll.
Fielding and running: fielders take positions by defence setting (Normal, Infield in, Deep); the sim solves interceptions with range, arm and glove, picks the target base, throws along arcs, resolves force and tag plays, double plays, errors and bad hops, tag-ups and sacrifice flies, foul balls, home runs robbed at the wall, steals (key T) and wild pitches, walks, strikeouts. Runners follow real base paths with leads and slides.
Pitching side: choose pitch type (Mix, Fast, Slide, Curve, Change), target (Mix, Zone, Corners, Chase), defence, and change pitchers from a drop-down. The AI manager handles the side you do not manage.
Flow: ceremony and line-ups, innings with an inning-break caption, play descriptions after every ball in play, final result with the walk-off note. Auto-next game option.

UI
On the canvas: a broadcast bug (inning, outs, count, runners on a diamond, scores, current batter and pitcher with pitch count), pitch speed and type read-out, captions for big plays, a challenge button with a countdown and the "eye" overlay, a swing button for touch.
Panel: game length, team pickers, which team you manage, new game, skip ceremony, speed (1/2x, 1x, 2x, 4x), auto-next, pause; surface, wind, time of day, floodlight state; coach controls for batting or fielding; camera (TV follow, Behind plate, Island), rotate, zoom, pixel size, outline / dither / raw / sound / lift toggles; box score for both teams, play-by-play feed.
Keys: Space swing (manual) or pause, N new game, K skip, P pause, C challenge, T steal, S surface, W wind, L light, Q/E rotate, +/- zoom, R reset the view, 1-3 cameras. Phone: coach controls and swing button docked under the canvas, no horizontal scroll. Procedural WebAudio (bat crack, mitt pop, crowd roar, groans).

QUALITY BAR
Headless bot test: full 9-inning games finish with plausible lines (roughly 3-10 runs a side, a few home runs, some errors, a few steals), no stuck states, no console errors, no horizontal scroll on a phone, no holes in the island from any camera angle.
No personal data, keys or paths in the source; the only external requests are the three.js script and Google Fonts.
